title: Keep the audit log fast all day and exportable at any time

blocks.text: Every request to the back office appends an event to `AuditLog`: who did what, numbered in order. By the end of a day the log holds tens of thousands of events. Compliance can start an export at any moment; it walks the log and writes each event to the archive, which takes a few milliseconds per event, while requests keep arriving.

Ops wants three things from the log. Request latency must not creep up as the day's log grows. A request must never wait for an export that happens to be running. An export must finish, with every event that was in the log when it began, once each and in order; whether it also includes events appended while it runs doesn't matter.
Finish `src/main/java/practice/AuditLog.java`: choose the collection in `newStore()`, and write `store` and `export`. About six lines in total.

cases.says: an export hands every appended event to the archive once, in the order of appends
an append to a log of 20,000 events allocates about what one stored event needs, not a copy of the log
an append from a request thread returns while an export is still writing to the archive
an export that runs while events are appended completes, with every earlier event once and in order

origin.section: A Weakly Consistent Walk Fits Work on One Element at a Time, Not a Total Across Elements

concepts: Every write to a CopyOnWriteArrayList copies the whole array, so time and allocation per write grow with the list's size.
A weakly consistent walk fits work that handles each element on its own: it takes no lock, never fails, and writers go on during it.
